newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen climbing on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen climbing on U.S. data.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to rally on Tuesday on an unexpectedly small rise in the closely watched U.S. employment cost index which was seen likely to quell inflation fears.
"I think they're going up but Toronto will lag (New York)," said one trader.
He said any indication that the U.S. economic engine is beginning to rev at a slower rate could bode ill for Canada whose economy has yet to hit top speed.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index edged up 0.30 points to 5835.61.
The U.S. employment cost index rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, compared with economists' expectations of a 0.9 percent increase.

The index is a closely watched indicator of inflation and traders said growing interest rate worries should be soothed by such a muted rise. Interest-sensitive shares in the United States and Canada such as banks and conglomerates were seen likely to profit from the reduction in rate jitters.
Canadian department stores sales rose a seasonally adjusted 0.7 percent in March from February to C$1.29 billion.
